definitions.explanation: The act of sending out goods from a warehouse or production facility to be delivered.

examples.japanese: {本日|ほんじつ}{出荷|しゅっか}しました。
{出荷|しゅっか}{準備|じゅんび}が{完了|かんりょう}した。
{注文|ちゅうもん}を{受|う}けてから3{日|にち}で{出荷|しゅっか}できます。
examples.english: We can ship within three days of receiving the order.

notes:
{出荷|しゅっか} refers to sending goods out from a warehouse or factory. It is a business/logistics term covering the dispatch side of the supply chain.

WORD FORMATION:
{出|しゅつ} (out) + {荷|か} (cargo, goods). Literally "sending out the goods."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {出荷|しゅっか}する: to ship
- {出荷|しゅっか}{準備|じゅんび}: shipping preparation
- {出荷|しゅっか}{予定|よてい}{日|び}: scheduled shipping date
- {出荷|しゅっか}{台数|だいすう}: number of units shipped
- {出荷|しゅっか}{停止|ていし}: shipment suspension

CONTRAST:
- {出荷|しゅっか}: shipping out from warehouse/factory
- {入荷|にゅうか}: arrival of goods (receiving stock)
- {納品|のうひん}: delivery to the customer
- {配送|はいそう}: delivery, transport to destination
- {発送|はっそう}: dispatching (parcels, mail)
